name: Joshua Tree and the Coachella Valley

cities.base: The half mile of Twentynine Palms Highway around Park Boulevard, or a rental off Sunfair Road north of town. Stay within ten minutes of the West Entrance, whose queue runs 30 to 45 minutes.
cities.name: Joshua Tree

cities.base: Along Utah Trail or National Park Drive near the Oasis of Mara. Plainer and cheaper than Joshua Tree, it is a Marine base town, and it puts you at the North Entrance, closest to the Pinto Basin road.
cities.name: Twentynine Palms

cities.base: Either the Pioneertown Road side above Yucca Valley, for the Pappy's and Red Dog end of things, or down near Highway 62 for groceries and the Black Rock trailheads. This is where the supermarkets are.
cities.name: Yucca Valley and Pioneertown

cities.base: The Uptown Design District on North Palm Canyon, or the Movie Colony just east of downtown. Both let you walk to dinner, which nowhere else on this trip does. Summer rates fall by half.
cities.name: Palm Springs

cities.base: No beds except campgrounds, no fuel, no water beyond the visitor centers, and no phone signal. You drive in from Joshua Tree town or Twentynine Palms and you drive back out.
cities.name: The park interior: Hidden Valley to Keys View

cities.base: The low Colorado Desert end of the park, 1,000 feet lower and hotter than the Joshua tree country. A visitor center, a campground, two good trails and nothing else.
cities.name: Cottonwood and the south end of the park

places.name: Joshua Tree Visitor Center
places.note: On Park Boulevard just south of Highway 62, outside the gate, 08:00 to 17:00 daily by an older NPS page, so confirm. NPS sells passes here but does not say entry is free, so check the price; fill water bottles, there is none inside the park.

places.name: Joshua Tree Coffee Company
places.note: They roast on site and they open at seven, which matters when you are trying to be at a trailhead by half past. Order ahead online on weekends.

places.name: Crossroads Cafe
places.note: The default breakfast in town for climbers and everybody else, so expect a 30 minute wait after 9am. Good vegetarian cooking, closes at 2:30pm, no dinner.
places.neighborhood: Twentynine Palms Highway at Park Boulevard

places.name: Sky High Pie
places.note: Pizza and a patio, useful because so little in Joshua Tree town serves food after 8pm. Hours drift seasonally, so call before driving over.

places.name: Royal Siam Cuisine
places.note: Unremarkable room, genuinely competent Thai, and almost never full. This is the one locals send you to when Crossroads has shut for the day.

places.name: Sam's Indian Food and Pizza
places.note: Curry and pizza from the same kitchen, which sounds wrong and works. Order the curry. It is a strip mall unit with about four tables, so plan on takeaway.

places.name: Mas o Menos
places.note: Tacos and a shaded yard on the drive between Yucca Valley and Joshua Tree. A reasonable lunch stop when you come off a morning hike and do not want to sit indoors.
places.neighborhood: Highway 62, west of Joshua Tree village

places.name: Joshua Tree Saloon
places.note: A dive with a pool table, burgers and a karaoke night, roughly half locals and half people in new hiking boots. Not a destination, but it is open when everything else is not.

places.name: Noah Purifoy Outdoor Desert Art Museum
places.note: Ten acres of assemblage sculpture the artist built here from 1989 until his death, left to weather. Free, open sunup to sundown daily, last mile on dirt, and no shade whatsoever.
places.neighborhood: Blair Lane, five minutes north of town

places.name: Joshua Tree Retreat Center
places.note: Founded in 1927 by Ding Le Mei as the Institute of Mentalphysics, with buildings by Lloyd Wright completed in 1946. A working retreat centre, booked by email or phone, with vortex paths for a fee and no fixed hours, so check the price and access first.
places.neighborhood: Highway 62, west of town (59700 29 Palms Hwy)

places.name: West Entrance Station
places.note: The busiest of the three gates. Thirty dollars per vehicle for seven days, or 55 for the annual pass. Buy on recreation.gov beforehand and save the pass to your phone, because there is no signal in the queue.
places.neighborhood: Park Boulevard, five miles south of town

places.name: Joshua Tree National Park Visitor Center
places.note: The main park centre on Freedom Way, bigger and less frantic than the one in Joshua Tree town, with the Universal Threads exhibit and the backcountry permit desk. Open 08:00 to 17:00; NPS does not state a price for the centre, so check the price.

places.name: Oasis of Mara
places.note: A half-mile paved loop through the fan palm spring the Serrano lived at, which is why the town exists at all. Flat, shaded, and the one park walk that works in July.

places.name: Fortynine Palms Oasis Trail
places.note: Three miles over a ridge to a palm grove with a trickle of water in it. Closed by the park June 1 to September 30 every year because of heat incidents. No shade until you arrive.
places.neighborhood: Canyon Road, west of Twentynine Palms

places.name: The Oasis of Murals
places.note: Around two dozen large murals of local history painted on downtown buildings since 1994. The free brochure from the visitor centre is the only way to find them in order.

places.name: Sky's The Limit Observatory and Nature Center
places.note: Volunteer-run observatory with a meditation garden and free public star parties, usually on Saturdays near new moon. Check their calendar before turning up, the schedule is not fixed.
places.neighborhood: Utah Trail, by the park's north entrance

places.name: Smith's Ranch Drive-In
places.note: One screen, Friday and Saturday only, box office at 7pm and the film at 7:30. Sound comes through your car radio. Bring cash and a blanket, it gets cold by the second reel.

places.name: The Restaurant at the 29 Palms Inn
places.note: Dinner on a patio beside the palm oasis, with vegetables from their own garden. Closed Monday and Tuesday, kitchen shuts at 8:30, and reservations matter on weekends.
places.neighborhood: Inn Avenue, on the Oasis of Mara

places.name: Kitchen in the Desert
places.note: Caribbean cooking and serious cocktails in a yard with a firepit, and the best dinner in the high desert outside Pappy's. Book ahead; it is small and the town knows.

places.name: The Rib Co.
places.note: Barbecue, booths, and a crowd that is mostly Marines and their families. Nobody comes to the desert for it, but it is reliable and it is open when the nicer places are booked.

places.name: Old Schoolhouse Museum
places.note: The 1927 schoolhouse, run by the historical society, on homesteading and the veterans sent here after the First World War for the dry air. Free, donations welcome; 13:00 to 16:00, Friday to Sunday by one source and Wednesday to Sunday by another, so check hours.

places.name: Pappy & Harriet's
places.note: Open daily 11am to 11pm, last dinner seating 9:30. The barbecue is fine, the room is the point, and the booking calendar is the only thing that decides whether tonight is worth the drive.

places.name: Mane Street, Pioneertown
places.note: A 1946 western film set built by Roy Rogers and Gene Autry that people then moved into. Two blocks long, a handful of shops, and done in half an hour unless there is a gunfight show on.

places.name: The Red Dog Saloon
places.note: Tex-Mex two hundred yards from Pappy's: brisket or carnitas tacos at $5, queso $8, so three tacos and queso run about $23 (live menu, undated). Open 10:00 to 22:00, to midnight Friday and Saturday and from 09:00 at weekends.

places.name: La Copine
places.note: The best cooking in the high desert, out on a highway with nothing around it. Thursday to Sunday, 11 to 4 only. Text for a reservation weeks ahead or queue outside in the sun.
places.neighborhood: Flamingo Heights, Old Woman Springs Road

places.name: The Integratron
places.note: A 60 minute crystal bowl sound bath in George Van Tassel's 1950s wooden dome. Wednesday to Saturday, books out a month ahead, and it closed 5 July to 9 September in 2026 for restoration.

places.name: Giant Rock
places.note: A seven-storey freestanding boulder, sacred to the Serrano, site of 1950s UFO conventions, and now covered end to end in spray paint. Four miles of washboard dirt each way for a defaced rock.

places.name: Gubler Orchids
places.note: A commercial orchid greenhouse in the middle of the Mojave, five dollars for the tour, Wednesday to Saturday. Closed-toe shoes required or they will turn you away at the door.

places.name: Hi-Desert Nature Museum
places.note: Small, free, town-run, with a live reptile room and good desert geology displays. Wednesday to Saturday only. A sensible hour when it is 112F outside.

places.name: The Tiny Pony Tavern
places.note: Art-covered bar with a scratch kitchen and a dog-friendly patio: the Tiny Pony Burger is $16 and fries $8, about $24 a head (own menu, undated). Open 11:00 to 01:00, from 09:00 for weekend brunch; the late option when Pioneertown has shut.

places.name: Panorama Loop from Black Rock Canyon
places.note: Six and a half miles through the densest Joshua tree stands in the park, from a trailhead you reach without paying an entrance station. The nature center runs reduced Thursday to Sunday hours in summer.
places.neighborhood: Black Rock Canyon Road, south Yucca Valley

places.name: Pioneertown Mountains Preserve
places.note: Twenty-five thousand acres, free, sunrise to sunset, and usually empty. Indian Loop and Sawtooth Loop are the two open trails. Park at the Kees Road lot, not the old Chaparrosa Wash entrance.

places.name: Palm Springs Aerial Tramway
places.note: Rotating cars from 2,600 to 8,500 feet and about 35 degrees cooler at the top. Around 37 dollars adult. It closes for roughly a month of maintenance each September, so check before you plan a day on it.

places.name: Palm Springs Art Museum
places.note: Strong on desert modernism and postwar California art, in a 1976 Williams building. Thursday 12:00 to 20:00 (free 17:00 to 20:00), Friday to Sunday 10:00 to 17:00, $25 adults, free under 18; Mondays open from 23 November 2026.

places.name: Moorten Botanical Garden
places.note: A family cactus garden going since 1938, with a greenhouse Cactarium. Seven dollars. October to May it runs 10 to 4 closed Wednesdays; June to September it drops to 9am to 1pm, Friday to Sunday only.

places.name: Palm Canyon at the Indian Canyons
places.note: The largest California fan palm oasis anywhere, with shade and running water. Twelve dollars, 8 to 5, last vehicle in at 4. Friday to Sunday only from 6 July to 1 October.
places.neighborhood: South Palm Canyon Drive, Agua Caliente land

places.name: Tahquitz Canyon
places.note: A two-mile loop to a 60-foot waterfall inside the city limits. Fifteen dollars, last entry 3:30. In July to September it opens Friday to Sunday only and runs one ranger hike, at 8am.

places.name: Cheeky's
places.note: The breakfast everyone tells you about, menu changed weekly, bacon flight and all. Thursday to Monday, 8 to 2. No reservations and the line forms before they open.

places.name: VillageFest
places.note: Thursday nights only, when they close Palm Canyon Drive for a street market of produce, craft stalls and food carts. Summer hours shift later; the city publishes the change each June.

places.name: Bootlegger Tiki
places.note: A dark red 24-seat tiki room on the site of Don the Beachcomber's old bar. Opens at 3pm, happy hour in the first and last hour, and it closes Tuesday and Wednesday through summer.

places.name: Melvyn's at the Ingleside Estate
places.note: Steak Diane flamed at the table in a room Sinatra drank in, recently restored. You are paying for the continuity, not the cooking. Book, and do not turn up in hiking clothes.

places.name: Palm Springs Air Museum
places.note: One of the larger collections of flyable Second World War aircraft anywhere, with veteran volunteers who talk you through them. Daily 10 to 5, 24 dollars, and the hangars are air conditioned.
places.neighborhood: Gene Autry Trail, by the airport

places.name: Sunnylands Center and Gardens
places.note: The Annenberg estate's public gardens, free, Wednesday to Sunday 8:30 to 4. Shut entirely from early June to mid-September. House tours are separately ticketed and sell out fast.

places.name: The Living Desert Zoo and Gardens
places.note: Desert species from four continents on 1,200 acres. Forty-five dollars is steep. June to September it opens 7am and shuts at 1:30pm, which is the only sane way to do it.

places.name: McCallum Trail, Coachella Valley Preserve
places.note: Two miles of boardwalk and sand to a palm grove sitting directly on the San Andreas fault, which is what pushes the water up. Free. The visitor centre is a 1930s palm-log cabin.

places.name: Ryan Mountain
places.note: Three miles, 1,050 feet, all of it rock steps and none of it shaded. The summit view over Queen Valley and Pleasant Valley is the best in the park. Do it first thing or not at all.

places.name: Hidden Valley Nature Trail
places.note: A one-mile loop inside a rock-walled bowl that cattle rustlers supposedly used as a corral. The best short introduction to the geology, and the car park is full by 9am on weekends.

places.name: Barker Dam Loop
places.note: A flat 1.3-mile loop past a cattle dam from 1900 and a petroglyph panel that was regrettably painted over by a film crew in the 1950s. The reservoir is usually dry.

places.name: Keys View
places.note: Five thousand feet straight down onto the Coachella Valley, the Salton Sea and the San Andreas fault. Crowded at sunset and genuinely windy and cold up there. Valley haze often kills the long view.

places.name: Cholla Cactus Garden
places.note: A quarter-mile boardwalk through dense teddy bear cholla at the Mojave to Colorado Desert transition. Backlit at sunrise it is the best photograph in the park. The spines detach on contact.

places.name: Skull Rock
places.note: A boulder with two eye sockets, six feet from a road with no real parking, and a permanent queue of people waiting to stand in front of it. The nearby 1.7-mile loop is better than the rock.

places.name: Arch Rock via Twin Tanks
places.note: A flat 1.4 miles from the Twin Tanks lot to a granite arch, through boulder piles most people drive past. Park at Twin Tanks, not at White Tank campground, which is closed June to August.
places.neighborhood: Pinto Basin Road, near White Tank

places.name: Stargazing at Jumbo Rocks
places.note: Certified dark sky, and on a moonless night the Milky Way casts a shadow. Sit on warm rock away from headlights. Temperatures drop 30F after sunset, and there is no phone signal if you get lost.

places.name: Keys Ranch
places.note: Ranger-led only, half a mile on foot, two hours, typically October to May. Twenty dollars adult, ten people maximum, booked on recreation.gov up to 60 days ahead. The homestead is left as the family had it.
places.neighborhood: Off Park Boulevard, behind a locked gate

places.name: Split Rock Loop
places.note: Two and a half miles of easy loop past Face Rock and some of the better boulder piles, with a fraction of the traffic of the nearby trails. Short dirt access road, fine in any car.
places.neighborhood: Off Park Boulevard, east of Jumbo Rocks

places.name: Lost Horse Mine
places.note: Four miles to the best-preserved ten-stamp mill in the park, which produced real gold between 1894 and 1931. Exposed the whole way, and the last mile of access road is dirt.

places.name: Cap Rock
places.note: A flat, accessible half-mile loop, and the place Gram Parsons' body was taken and burned in 1973. Fans still leave things. Good, quick, and the car park is dark enough for stars.
places.neighborhood: Junction of Park Boulevard and Keys View Road

places.name: Wall Street Mill
places.note: A flat mile and a half past abandoned cars and a windmill to Bill Keys' gold mill, with the marker for the man he shot here in 1943. No booking, unlike his ranch.

places.name: Cottonwood Visitor Center
places.note: The smallest of the park's four centres and the last water and toilets before the south end trails, 08:30 to 16:00. NPS states no price for the centre, so check the price; it sits inside the park, so the $30 vehicle fee applies to reach it.
places.neighborhood: Pinto Basin Road, seven miles north of I-10

places.name: Cottonwood Spring Oasis
places.note: Fan palms and cottonwoods at a Cahuilla water source that later served the gold mills, five minutes from the car. Arrastras and mill remains sit just off the path.

places.name: Lost Palms Oasis Trail
places.note: Seven and a half miles round trip, 500 feet of gain, five to six hours, to the largest palm grove in the park. This is the hike people get into trouble on. November to March only.

places.name: Mastodon Peak Loop
places.note: Three miles and 375 feet, past the Mastodon gold mine to a scramble summit looking at the Salton Sea. The sensible substitute when Lost Palms is too long or too hot.

places.name: Bajada Nature Trail
places.note: A quarter-mile signed loop on the alluvial fan, explaining the low Colorado Desert plants you have been driving past. Twenty minutes, and the first thing you hit coming in from I-10.
places.neighborhood: Pinto Basin Road, near the south entrance

places.name: Shields Date Garden
places.note: Date shakes, a date grove you can walk, and a 1950s film called Romance and Sex Life of the Date that plays on a loop. The obvious stop on the drive back from Cottonwood.

places.name: Salton Sea State Recreation Area
places.note: A shrinking accidental lake 230 feet below sea level, with beaches made of fish bones and a smell on hot days. Seven dollars per car. Go for the bird life and the strangeness, not for a swim.

places.name: World Famous Crochet Museum
places.note: Shari Elf turned an old one-hour photo hut into an acid-green kiosk full of crocheted things in 2006. Free, donations welcome, 10:00 to 18:00 daily, and 20 minutes is plenty.

places.name: Beauty Bubble Salon & Museum
places.note: A working salon holding Jeff Hafler's collection of over 3,000 vintage beauty artifacts. Wednesday to Saturday 10:00 to 18:00, Sunday 11:00 to 16:00, closed Monday and Tuesday; one reviewer says it is free, so check the price.

places.name: Desert View Conservation Area
places.note: Lightly used boulder trails just south of town, free, 07:00 to 19:00 daily. The trails are poorly marked and there is only a pit toilet, so bring water and go early morning or late afternoon.

places.name: Murtle the Turtle Sculpture
places.note: A giant stone turtle in a roadside parking lot, a nod to the desert tortoise; climbing is at your own risk. Hours and price are not listed, so treat it as a ten-minute stop on the way past.

places.name: Joshua Tree Rock Shop
places.note: A minerals and fossils shop on the highway, 10:00 to 18:00 daily, 4.7 on 237 Google reviews. No admission is stated; it is a shop, so 20 minutes unless you are buying.

places.name: "Transmission" Sculpture by Daniel Popper
places.note: Daniel Popper's mirrored-glass sculpture on private land, seen behind a fence at the end of a bumpy dirt road, about 20 km from town. Hours and price are not listed, so check the price, and go early or off-peak.

places.name: Indian Cove Nature Trail
places.note: An easy half-mile interpretive loop with signs on desert plants and indigenous history. No separate fee, but it is inside the park so the $30 vehicle fee applies; little shade, so go early or late.
places.neighborhood: Indian Cove, north side of the park

places.name: Desert Christ Park
places.note: More than 40 religious statues by Antone Martin on 3.5 acres, begun in the mid 1940s and opened in 1951, left to decay during an ACLU suit from 1988 to 1996, then restored. Free, 07:00 to 18:00 daily; no restrooms or food nearby.

places.name: Big Morongo Canyon Preserve
places.note: A desert oasis of springs 15 km west of Yucca Valley, free, 07:30 to 18:30 daily, with a wheelchair-accessible boardwalk on the Marsh Trail and guided bird walks on Wednesday and Saturday. No pets and little shade.

places.name: Sherman's Deli & Bakery
places.note: The town's deli, 4.6 on 8,275 Google reviews: cheeseburger deluxe $23.95, meatloaf dinner $24.95, two eggs $15.95 on the October 2025 menu. Open 08:00 to 21:00 daily, so it covers breakfast on the days Cheeky's is shut.

places.name: Rooster and the Pig
places.note: Vietnamese plates for sharing: shaking beef $17, five spice chicken $16, sea bass $21, starters $10 to $14, so about $29 a head (undated menu, prices may have moved). Wednesday to Sunday 17:00 to 21:00.

places.name: Agua Caliente Cultural Museum
places.note: Founded in 1991 and the first Native American museum in the Smithsonian Affiliations Program: two galleries, 1 to 2 hours. Timed entry, last at 16:00, closed Mondays; the adult price is not published, so check the price.

places.name: Cornelia White House and McCallum Adobe
places.note: The 1893 house built of reused Palmdale Railroad ties, beside the 1884 McCallum Adobe. The house opens weekends and the adobe most days, so hours vary, check, and check the price: the historical society reported repairs this November and a 9 November reopening, so call 760-323-8297.
places.neighborhood: Village Green, 221 S Palm Canyon Drive

places.name: Tramway Gas Station (Palm Springs Visitor Center)
places.note: Albert Frey and Robson Chambers' 1965 gas station, the Palm Springs Visitor Center since 2003, on the road to the tram. Hours and price are not listed, so check the price; half an hour is enough.

outings.why: Three miles and 1,050 feet of stone staircase to the best 360 in the park. It is short and it is relentless, with no shade at any point, so it is a first-light hike from April onward or not a hike at all.
outings.name: Ryan Mountain
outings.season: All year, but start by 06:30 May to September
outings.fallback: Cap Rock loop at the bottom of the same road, half a mile and flat.

outings.why: A quarter-mile boardwalk loop through ten acres of teddy bear cholla at the seam where the Mojave drops into the Colorado Desert. The light at sunrise is why people drive 40 minutes in the dark for it. Do not touch anything.
outings.name: the Cholla Cactus Garden at sunrise
outings.season: All year. It has closed for trail work in past winters, so c
outings.fallback: Arch Rock from the Twin Tanks lot, 20 minutes closer and also good early.

outings.why: The two easy loops that show you what the rock formations actually are, plus the petroglyph panel at Barker Dam. Both lots fill by 9am on weekends and there is no overflow parking.
outings.name: Hidden Valley and Barker Dam
outings.fallback: Skip Barker Dam and just walk Hidden Valley, which takes 45 minutes.

outings.why: Keys View looks down 5,000 feet onto the Coachella Valley and the San Andreas fault trace, and then you drive 40 minutes east to sit on granite under one of the darkest skies in southern California. Bring layers, it drops 30 degrees after d
outings.name: Keys View at sunset, then Jumbo Rocks for the stars
outings.season: All year. Avoid the three nights either side of a full moon.
outings.fallback: Cap Rock parking area, which is five minutes from Keys View and dark enough.

outings.why: Three miles over a ridge to a real fan palm oasis with no road to it. The park closes this trail June 1 to September 30 every year specifically because people get heatstroke on it.
outings.name: Fortynine Palms Oasis
outings.fallback: The Oasis of Mara boardwalk behind the Twentynine Palms visitor center, flat and shaded.

outings.why: Seven and a half miles out and back through washes to the largest palm grove in the park, from the south entrance an hour east of Palm Springs on I-10. The drive is most of why it takes a full day. Carry four litres each.
outings.name: Lost Palms Oasis from Cottonwood
outings.season: November to March. Do not attempt it April to October.
outings.fallback: Mastodon Peak loop from the same trailhead, three miles.

outings.why: A ranger walks you half a mile around the homestead the Keys family held from 1917 to 1969, still full of their machinery. Two hours, 20 dollars, ten people maximum, and you must book on recreation.gov ahead of time.
outings.name: the Keys Ranch tour
outings.fallback: Wall Street Mill, a flat mile and a half to the same family's stamp mill, no booking.

outings.why: Ten minutes of rotating cable car takes you from 2,600 feet to 8,500 feet and about 35 degrees cooler, into pine forest with 50 miles of trail. The queue on a summer weekend can be two hours, and it shuts for maintenance for roughly a month
outings.name: the tram to Long Valley
outings.season: All year except the annual September maintenance closure
outings.fallback: Drive up to Idyllwild instead, which takes longer but never queues.

outings.why: Fifteen miles of trail on Agua Caliente land through the largest California fan palm oasis in the world, with actual shade and actual water. From July 6 to October 1 it opens Friday to Sunday only, 8am to 5pm.
outings.name: Palm Canyon in the Indian Canyons
outings.season: All year, Friday to Sunday only in high summer
outings.fallback: Tahquitz Canyon, a two-mile loop to a 60-foot waterfall, same ownership and ticketing.

outings.why: A barbecue joint in a 1940s film set that books touring bands who have no business playing a 300-capacity room. Open 11am to 11pm daily, but tickets for the good nights sell out weeks ahead and the restaurant wait can be 90 minutes without
outings.name: Pappy and Harriet's on a show night
outings.fallback: The Red Dog Saloon 200 yards up Mane Street, no ticket needed.

outings.why: An hour lying on the floor of a 1950s domed structure built by a man who said aliens told him how, while someone plays 22 quartz bowls. It sells out a month ahead, runs Wednesday to Saturday, and closed entirely July 5 to September 9 in 202
outings.name: the Integratron sound bath and Giant Rock
outings.season: September to early July, Wednesday to Saturday
outings.fallback: Gubler Orchids down the same road, a 5 dollar greenhouse tour, Wednesday to Saturday.

destination.name: Joshua Tree and the Coachella Valley
destination.pitch: Two deserts stacked on top of each other, one hour apart: granite and Joshua trees up at 4,000 feet, palm oases and mid-century swimming pools down on the valley floor.
destination.caveat: From June to September the valley floor runs 110F to 118F and the park 100F to 110F, which turns every hike into a pre-dawn job and shuts things: Fortynine Palms Oasis trail closes June 1 to September 30, Sunnylands closes for the summer, and the Integratron closed July 5 to September 9 in 2026. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Palm Springs is the only urban thing here and it is small; you will exhaust downtown in an afternoon.
because.food: Honest but thin: a handful of good kitchens in the high desert, a real restaurant town in Palm Springs, and long stretches with nothing but gas station burritos.
because.nature: Two distinct deserts meet inside one park boundary, so you can walk through Joshua tree forest at breakfast and cholla at the Colorado Desert transition by mid-morning.
because.culture: Noah Purifoy's assemblage yard, the Integratron, Pioneertown and Palm Springs modernism are all one strange desert story told four ways.
because.adventure: Rock climbing on the park's granite, night skies dark enough to see the Milky Way from a roadside pullout, and enough exposure risk that the heat has to be planned around.
because.relaxation: Palm Springs is built around pools and shade, and a rented house with a pool in Yucca Valley costs less than a hotel room in most cities.
because.exploration: The interesting things are scattered down dirt roads and along a 40-mile highway, so a car and a loose plan get you further than any itinerary.
